boot.evidence: Seven real guest boots, all through the launcher with no runit: each run's kernel release is read from the GUEST's own uname (g169b17ff3f66 for the pin, g32e5e10b81d8 for HEAD), so a run can never be attributed to the wrong kernel. Every run reached BENCH_START and powered off via the guest (poweroff -f).

bench_harness.evidence: bench/bench.sh boots one guest per run, waits for the guest's own BENCH_DONE marker before tearing down, and bench/summarise.py emits median + range per (kernel, profile) as summary.json/summary.md. The three profiles are fork-exec (1500 x /bin/true), page-fault heavy (512 MiB read at bs=4k = one fault per page) and sequential disk read (1 GiB, READ-ONLY on /dev/ubda, so the benchmark cannot disturb an image or a digest baseline).

a1_verdict.evidence: A first pin-vs-HEAD campaign completed (>=3 runs per cell after one cold first run blew past the wait window and was re-run), but the result is DIRECTIONAL, not decision-grade: fork-exec is equivalent (head 43430 ms vs pin 44625 ms, within 5%), fault-heavy reads favour HEAD (head 1180 ms median vs pin 1545 ms, median-based -30.9%, and HEAD's best run 1120 ms is below pin's best 1400 ms), disk read also favours HEAD by median (5580 vs 6169 ms) but HEAD has a 127 s outlier in that cell. Recorded ok=false because a pin decision cannot be taken from it: load average on the device was 16-20 during the campaign (other work running in parallel) and per-cell spread reached 30-2200%, which is larger than the median differences.

head_257d23ee_hypothesis.evidence: The A1 hypothesis (upstream 257d23ee, 'give libc back what it allocated inside physical memory', lowers fault cost) is CONSISTENT with the fault-heavy cell here: HEAD is faster at the median and at the best case, while fork-exec is unchanged - which is what a fault-path improvement should look like. It is NOT confirmed: the spread is 79% (pin) and 224% (HEAD) on that cell, so the effect is smaller than the measurement noise on this device.

bench_noise.evidence: Honest limitation, recorded as a defect of the measurement, not of a component: the campaign ran while the device was loaded (load average 16-20). Values inside one cell ranged 3410-127150 ms (HEAD disk read) and 1120-3760 ms (HEAD pagefault). Any decision-grade repetition needs a quiet device, a discarded warm-up run per kernel, and more runs per cell.

notes: Direction A (docs/NEXT-STEPS.md). README/contract were not touched by this run. The release pin stays 169b17ff: this campaign does not justify moving it, and no HEAD release has been cut.
known_limits_observed: runs per kernel are not equal for every profile (pin has 4 values on two profiles because one cold run was re-run)
one guest run (pin-1) never reached its disk-read result inside the wait window; it was re-run with a longer BENCH_WAIT and both facts are kept in the artifacts
the benchmark is guest-only: host-side costs (Android app scheduling, thermal throttling) are not controlled
